newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile May supermarket sales rise 5.8 pct vs yr ago.
newsitem.headline: Chile May supermarket sales rise 5.8 pct vs yr ago.

text.p: Chilean supermarket sales in May were 5.8 percent higher than in the same month last year, an industry trade group said Wednesday.
Sales in the first five months of the year were 2.4 percent higher than sales for the corresponding period of 1996, the Chilean Supermarket Association said in a statement.
"The May figure shows that the (economic) adjustment process is starting to have less impact," it said.
The central bank's restrictive monetary policy, aimed at cooling consumer demand and damping inflation, has held back supermarket sales during the past year.
Chileans are among Latin America's most enthusiastic supermarket shoppers, and supermarket sales are widely regarded as a barometer of consumer spending.
